title: ARC and Memory
tagline: Who owns this object, and when does it go
summary: Automatic reference counting from the ground up — what memory is, why something has to decide when an object dies, and how Swift made the compiler do it. Answers the questions that stay confusing: why ARC isn't a garbage collector, why an object can die before the end of its scope, what weak actually costs, and why a retain cycle is a design mistake rather than a bug.
